title_en: RE-RELEASE: Texas Trend Following with Salem Abraham
title_zh: 德州趋势跟踪：与 Salem Abraham 重谈趋势交易（重发集）
subtitle_zh: 趋势传奇 Salem Abraham 讲述从德州小镇到期货交易的历程与全组合配置思路。
summary_zh: 本期 The Derivative 是一集重发（re-release），Jeff Malec 对话趋势跟踪（trend following）传奇、Abraham Trading Group 创始人 Salem Abraham。Abraham 扎根德州狭长地带仅 2500 人的小镇 Canadian，节目从他的牧场与果园讲起——他把这些视作一种'实物形态的固定收益'，以对冲交易员'撑死或饿死'的收入波动。他回顾自己从 Notre Dame 毕业后于 1988 年入行、一直交易到 2019 年 1 月的职业生涯：基金规模最高达 6 亿美元、关门时仍有 2 亿多，并坦言对冲基金行业费率与竞争日益艰难。他特别强调市场电子化如何拉平了非 Wall Street、非常春藤背景者的竞争场地，也讲到约 4% 交易是对账差错单的低效往事。核心议题是他近年转向的全组合（total portfolio）思路——用一套整体框架而非仅另类投资那一部分来抵御'风暴'，并主张以长达 70 年的投资生涯尺度来思考需要为冲击防护多久。是一集兼具交易史与配置哲学的深谈。

Today's special guest is someone who anyone familiar with the history of managed futures will know well, with many stories from being far removed from Wall Street and LaSalle Street, to extensive work with nonprofits, to creating his own fund, he's got a lot to share.

turns.zh: 我们说的当然就是 Salem Abraham，以及他的 Abraham Trading Group——在趋势跟踪和期货市场上，它的历史几乎和你能找到的任何一家一样悠久。

turns.en: His newest venture finds him focusing a little more on the total portfolio, not just the alts part and weathering the storm for a total portfolio approach, which we'll get into.
turns.zh: 他最新的事业让他更多地聚焦于整个投资组合（total portfolio），而不只是另类投资（alts）那一部分，用一套全组合的思路去抵御风暴，这个我们待会儿会深入聊。

turns.en: So it's just sure to be entertaining and educational. So welcome Salem. We're so glad to have you with us. But Jeff, it's great to be here, here on The Derivative.
turns.zh: 所以这期一定既有趣又有料。欢迎 Salem，我们非常高兴你能来。Jeff，很高兴能来做客，来到 The Derivative。

turns.en: Thanks for having me. No worries. And so I've known you for a bit, having crossed paths at various conferences and whatnot. But let's give listeners a little more color on you outside of the trading world.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。别客气。我认识你也有一阵了，在各种会议上打过照面什么的。不过我们先给听众讲讲你在交易世界之外的另一面。

turns.en: You're down there in Canadian, Texas, right? Where in the world of Texas is that? So Canadian is a little town of 2,500 people, two stoplights.
turns.zh: 你人在德州的 Canadian，对吧？那地方到底在德州的哪个角落？Canadian 是个只有 2500 人、两个红绿灯的小镇。

turns.en: It's up in the panhandle at Top Square in the northeast corner, about 100 miles northeast of Amorello. It is a town that's ranching. The main industries are ranching.
turns.zh: 它在德州狭长地带（panhandle）的东北角，大约在 Amarillo 东北方向 100 英里处。这是个以牧场为主的镇子，主要产业就是畜牧。

turns.en: And then oil and gas. And so I had two great grandfathers settle here with Lebanese merchant and Irish rancher. And the Lebanese boys kept marrying Irish girls for a couple of generations.
turns.zh: 然后就是石油和天然气。我有两位曾祖父在这里落脚，一个是黎巴嫩商人，一个是爱尔兰牧场主。之后好几代，黎巴嫩家的小伙子不断娶爱尔兰家的姑娘。

turns.en: So yes. Really? They'll seem like an odd mixing, right? Oh, no. Well, the Lebanese are real mean and tough and the Irish have a good time. So it's a nice mix.
turns.zh: 所以，是的。真的？这俩搭配听起来挺奇特的吧？哦不。黎巴嫩人又凶又硬气，爱尔兰人会玩儿、爱热闹，所以这是很好的组合。

turns.en: And so you're far north. You're like further north than Oklahoma City. Right. Yeah, I know we're as far north as you can get in Texas. Right.
turns.zh: 所以你在很靠北的地方，比 Oklahoma City 还北。对。是啊，我们已经到了德州能到的最北边了。没错。

turns.en: Yeah. No, you go, if we go about 50 miles north, we're out of Texas. And then about 30 miles east, we're over into Oklahoma there too. So we're close to five other state capitals and we are at Austin, including Lincoln, Nebraska, so way north.
turns.zh: 是啊。往北走大概 50 英里就出了德州；往东走大概 30 英里也进了 Oklahoma。所以我们离另外五个州的州府都很近，包括我们自己的 Austin，还有内布拉斯加的 Lincoln，反正是非常靠北。

turns.en: Really? And so you spread out your roots there. You've got some farmland. You've got some ranch land. You've got some orchards. So tell us a little bit about all that.
turns.zh: 真的？所以你在那边扎下了根，有一些农田，有一些牧场，还有一些果园。给我们讲讲这些吧。

turns.en: No, yeah. Well, so out here in the country, everything's cheaper. So they just give this stuff away. So we're ranch land. And then I've gotten over the last 10 years or so into orchards more.
turns.zh: 是啊。在乡下这边，什么都便宜，这些地几乎是白送。所以我们有牧场。然后过去十年左右，我更多涉足果园。

turns.en: So I've got an apple orchard here in Canadian, then a peach orchard over in Oklahoma, and a pecan orchard down in Central Texas. And so just mainly is a source of fixed income for me.
turns.zh: 我在 Canadian 这儿有个苹果园，在 Oklahoma 有个桃子园，在德州中部有个碧根果园。对我来说，这些主要是一个固定收益（fixed income）的来源。

turns.en: That is so, you know, and I have some other real estate investments that are just really fixed income type. I don't like bonds as well. So but I like the fixed income component.
turns.zh: 就是这样。我还有另外一些房地产投资，也基本属于固定收益那一类。我也不喜欢债券。但我喜欢固定收益这个组成部分。

turns.en: And as a trader, you know, you kind of tend to you make money in lumpy ways and it's feast or famine. So to have that fixed income component is good.
turns.zh: 而且作为一个交易员，你赚钱往往是一阵一阵的，不是撑死就是饿死。所以能有这么一块固定收益是好事。

turns.en: But I'd rather have it in the form of kind of real commodities, not fiat money. So got it. And so I'm envisioning you like out there working the ranch and the orchards.
turns.zh: 不过我更愿意它是实实在在的商品形式，而不是法币。明白。所以我脑子里浮现的画面是你亲自在牧场和果园里干活。

turns.en: Is that the case or no? Not so much. I go out there when they let me. I usually break things or maybe hurt myself if I go out there too much.
turns.zh: 是这样吗？也不是。他们让我去我才去。我要是去太多，通常不是把东西弄坏，就是把自己弄伤。

turns.en: But no, but I do have, you know, I my kids, they'll keep honey bees and I help them with honey bees. So we've got honey bees out here. That's kind of fun.
turns.zh: 不过，我的孩子们养蜜蜂，我会帮他们打理。所以我们这边有蜜蜂，挺有意思的。

turns.en: And then we and then to go steal some apples or peaches when you're, you know, it's a minute, 45 seconds. If I go straight to work halfway across town, so I could swing out to the orchard and make it a five minute commute and still some peaches or apples on the way to work.
turns.zh: 然后嘛，顺路去『偷』点苹果或桃子。我直接去上班的话，横穿半个镇子也就 45 秒、一分钟的事，所以我可以绕去果园，把通勤变成五分钟，路上还能摘点桃子或苹果带去上班。

turns.en: So that's nice. Got it. And you've separated. You don't have the work compound as part of your house and everything. You've got a separate office.
turns.zh: 那挺好。明白。你把工作和生活分开了，办公区没有跟自家房子连在一起，你有单独的办公室。

turns.en: No, I'm in, I'm, yeah, no, I'm in. So my house is in the middle of town and then offices. Yes. Halfway across town, seven blocks away. So got it.
turns.zh: 对，我家在镇子中央，办公室则在镇子的另一头，隔七个街区。明白。

turns.en: And then it's been hard to separate Canadian from you for a while, right? Like you've helped to renovations and buildings and a bunch. Well, no.
turns.zh: 而且这些年来，很难把你和 Canadian 这个镇子分开来看，对吧？你帮忙搞翻修、盖楼什么的，做了一大堆。嗯，是的。

turns.en: Good for the town. Sure. Well, I've been real blessed, you know, financially. And I think, you know, when you look at a town and you look around, it's especially a small town you look around and there's really a group of, you know, a small group of people, maybe probably even 50 people that are going to, that really are able and willing to make a difference.
turns.zh: 对镇子是好事。当然。我在财务上一直很幸运、很蒙福。我觉得，当你看一个镇子、环顾四周，尤其是小镇，你会发现真正有能力也愿意去带来改变的人，其实就是那么一小撮，可能也就 50 个人左右。

turns.en: And so you, you know, you end up, people step up and do different things, what they can. And, you know, that's true of even running, you know, the local government, things like that.
turns.zh: 所以最后就是，大家各自站出来，力所能及地做不同的事。哪怕是把地方政府运转起来这种事，也是一样。

turns.en: And so, no, we try to help out where we can and do things, you know, invest in the community. And there's sometimes a return on investment that can't be measured in dollars.
turns.zh: 所以我们尽量在能帮上忙的地方出力，去做事，去投资这个社区。有时候那种投资回报，是没法用美元来衡量的。

turns.en: But, but yeah, the best job I don't get, Jeff, though, the best job in a small town, you know, isn't mayor or anything like that. It's, you want to be fire chief, fire chief.
turns.zh: 不过话说回来，Jeff，小镇上最好的那份差事我可不干——最好的差事其实不是镇长之类的，而是你想当消防队长（fire chief），消防队长。

turns.en: You get to, you get to drive a truck and talk on the radio and every little, every boy's dream, right? Yeah, no, and I'm not cool enough to be on the, on the fire department.
turns.zh: 你能开消防车、用对讲机说话，这简直是每个小男孩的梦想，对吧？是啊，可我还没酷到能进消防队的程度。

turns.en: There's 32 people and you, you got to be in the club and really cool. And so no, Scott Brewster, my friend, Scott gets to be fire chief. And so no, so I can start in a town that small.
turns.zh: 消防队就 32 个人，你得是那个圈子里的、够酷才行。所以，是我朋友 Scott Brewster 当上了消防队长。在那么小的镇子上，也就这样了。

turns.en: It's just all volunteer. I'm sure, right? Oh yeah. So the bell rings and they leave what they're doing and go grab a truck. You bet. No, that's right.
turns.zh: 我猜那全是志愿的吧？哦是的。铃声一响，他们放下手头的事就去开消防车。没错，就是这样。

turns.en: No, and with eight kids, you know, so my wife and I, we dated in high school here, then I went off to Notre Dame. Got a finance degree, came back and we, we've been married now almost 32.
turns.zh: 再说，我们有八个孩子。我和我太太是在这儿的高中谈的恋爱，后来我去 Notre Dame 读书，拿了金融学位，回来后我们结婚到现在差不多 32 年了。

turns.en: Let's see, yeah, 32 years this year and we have eight kids. So, you know, there's not as much to do in the country. So we had to make our own entertainment.
turns.zh: 我想想，对，今年满 32 年，我们有八个孩子。乡下没什么消遣，所以我们只能自己找乐子。

turns.en: And so we, so, but I was on school board. So school board is bad. I was on school board for 12 years. I could make everybody, you know, after 12 years, everyone's mad twice.
turns.zh: 我还在学区董事会（school board）待过。校董会可不是好差事。我干了 12 年，12 年下来，我能把每个人都得罪两轮。

turns.en: So it's time to get off there. They like you. They're mad at you. They like you. They're mad at you. Yeah, no, that's it. So eight kids, what's the spread there in the ages?
turns.zh: 所以是时候退下来了。他们喜欢你，又生你的气；喜欢你，又生你的气。是啊，就这么回事。那八个孩子，年龄跨度多大？

turns.en: So today there's really, there's, there's 10 years, 10 months, oldest, youngest. So, so there's seven, almost 17 on Saturday. It'll be 17 to almost 28.
turns.zh: 到今天，老大和老小之间正好差 10 年零 10 个月。我们有七个……最小的这周六就快 17 岁了，所以是从快 17 岁到快 28 岁。

turns.en: So this Saturday. So, so we got four brothers and two sisters in my world, but they're from many different fathers and mothers and mixtures, few divorces and stepmoms and stepdads.
turns.zh: 就这周六。在我这个大家庭里，有四个兄弟、两个姐妹，但他们来自不同的父母、不同的组合，有几次离异，也有继母继父。

turns.en: And yeah, I know everybody wonders if there's a trick and you're like, no, no trick. It was the two of us. There was no surrogates, no twins.
turns.zh: 是啊，我知道大家都好奇是不是有什么诀窍，我只能说没有诀窍，就是我们俩自己来的，没有代孕，也没有双胞胎。

turns.en: Just no, no Netflix. No, no, nothing, no, no multiple wives, multiple husbands, no adoptions. It's all, yeah. So what's the secret on 32 years of marriage?
turns.zh: 也没有 Netflix 可看。没有没有，什么都没有——没有多个妻子、多个丈夫，也没有领养，全是我们自己生的。是啊。那么，结婚 32 年的秘诀是什么？

turns.en: How do you, you got an algorithm for that? Or yeah, no, you, I have, it's crazy coupons. So everybody gets probably, I think it depends. Me, I need a few more extra crazy coupons in my wife.
turns.zh: 你对此有什么算法吗？有啊，我有——叫『发疯券』（crazy coupons）。每个人大概都能领几张，我觉得因人而异。我自己就需要比我太太多几张发疯券。

turns.en: She's less crazy than me. But if you can, if you can just say, look, you're allowed to have, say, you know, for me, four crazy coupons, you could be really crazy and make no sense on four things.
turns.zh: 她没我那么疯。但如果你能说：这样吧，比如给我四张发疯券，你就可以在四件事上特别不讲道理、特别任性。

turns.en: And I'm going to love you anyway. And so I think you just got to give them a pass on some things. And then it gets instead of trying to fix them.
turns.zh: 而我依然会爱你。所以我觉得，你就是得在某些事情上放对方一马，而不是老想着去改造他。

turns.en: You just say, you know, you're, you're fine, crazy and all. I like that. And then do they give the coupon? Then it gets ripped up or they can be crazy on the same thing for, for their home.
turns.zh: 你就说：你这样挺好的，疯就疯点，我喜欢。那这张券给了以后，是被撕掉作废，还是他们可以在同一件事上一直疯下去？

turns.en: Oh no, it's, it's pretty just one thing. You just say, no, this thing, but we're going to work on you elsewhere. There's some ways that, yeah, you'd like to try to fix them on some other spots.
turns.zh: 哦不，基本就是一事一券。你会说：这件事就算了，但别的地方我们还是得改造改造你。有些方面，是的，你会想在别的点上试着纠正对方。

turns.en: But no, we, I think you just got to say, all right, we've all got our, our crazy. And we're going to, and that's okay. So I love it. And then besides your work in the town, you're doing some, you've been heavily involved in a few different charities as well.
turns.zh: 不过我觉得，你就得认：好吧，我们每个人都有自己疯的一面，那就这样，也没关系。我很喜欢这个说法。那除了在镇上做的事，你还深度参与了好几个不同的慈善机构。

turns.en: Well, you know, I think being just, you know, in the land of the blind, the one I ban is keen. And, and so if you, if you know something about investments and there's, you know, there's foundations and endowments out here that need, you know, that need investment advice.
turns.zh: 嗯，你知道，在盲人国里，独眼龙就是国王。所以如果你懂点投资，而这儿又有一些基金会和捐赠基金（endowments）需要投资建议。

turns.en: So I get on a lot of investment committees and things like that. And so, so, yeah, so different foundations and endowments trying to help. And really and truly what you notice, you know, I know that, you know, there's this a red state, blue state and city and country and what, you know, I, I get to go to the city and I can put on my suit and I can take the subway in New York City.
turns.zh: 我就会加入很多投资委员会之类的。所以，是的，帮忙打理不同的基金会和捐赠基金。而且你真的会注意到——我知道有所谓红州蓝州、城市和乡村之分。我也会进城，穿上西装，在 New York City 坐地铁。

turns.en: I don't know my way around the city. Well, and I, but I've seen you in a suit. Yeah, that's right. Nice. Yeah. And so, but, you know, I always think they talk about a frog in a well.
turns.zh: 不过我可不认得城里的路。话说回来，我倒见过你穿西装的样子。是啊，没错。挺好。是啊。而且我总是想到那句『井底之蛙』。

turns.en: So frog, you know, you, you, you just know your own little world. And I think that's true of in today's society with politics, what they are, where you're in the country, you know, this country perspective.
turns.zh: 那只青蛙，就只知道自己那一小方天地。我觉得这在今天的社会、在政治上也是如此：你在乡下，就是乡下视角。

turns.en: And if you're in the city, you know, the city perspective, I think you need to know the tune and everything makes a lot more sense. Why people think what they do and out in the country, really and truly, I mean, you look around and it's like, if, if, you know, if you and I lived across the street from each other and there's no one within miles of us, you'd say, if we've got a problem, Jeff, you and I
turns.zh: 而你在城里，就是城里视角。我觉得你得把这些调子都摸清楚，很多事情才讲得通——才明白人们为什么会那样想。在乡下，说真的，环顾四周，就好比如果你和我住在街对面、方圆几英里都没有别人，你会说：Jeff，咱俩要是遇到了问题，

turns.en: have to figure it out and out in the country, that's what you've got to do. People have to step up because if you're, you know, if, if, if not, you know, this, this small group of people, then who, and it's nobody.
turns.zh: 就得自己想办法解决。在乡下就是这样，人必须站出来，因为如果不是这一小撮人来做，那还能有谁？没有了，谁都没有。

turns.en: And so you, you really, you, you step up and help. And so I've, I've done that. And then, and then that's led to some other things where, you know, now I'm on the investment committee at St. Jude Children's Research Hospital out of Memphis.
turns.zh: 所以你真的会站出来帮忙，我也这么做了。而这又带来了一些别的机会，比如现在我在孟菲斯的 St. Jude Children's Research Hospital（圣犹大儿童研究医院）的投资委员会任职。

turns.en: And so I've been, you know, from that, which is about a five billion endowment down to, you know, a $500,000 endowment. And then, and then I've done things with Boone Pickens and I, he's a neighbor.
turns.zh: 所以我参与过的捐赠基金，大的有大约 50 亿美元的，小的只有 50 万美元。我还和 Boone Pickens 一起做过一些事，他是我的邻居。

turns.en: He was a neighbor to us on a ranch and then he bought our ranch back in 08. And, but he and I have been friends for about 30 years. He was a friend of my grandfather's.
turns.zh: 他曾在牧场那边和我们做邻居，后来在 08 年把我们的牧场买了下来。不过我和他做了大概 30 年的朋友，他是我祖父的朋友。

turns.en: And so, and he's, his, his big ranch is right here near town. And so he and I started a foundation together back in 08. And that was the last one.
turns.zh: 他的大牧场就在镇子附近。所以我和他在 08 年一起创立了一个基金会，那是最后一个（我参与创立的）。

turns.en: Yeah. Best biography book name ever. The first billions of the hardest. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. No, and I'm in the book too. All right. I know the title, but I was in a Colorado once at a bar or restaurant or something talking with a guy and he's like, what are you doing in 10?
turns.zh: 是啊，史上最好的传记书名——《The First Billion Is the Hardest》。是啊是啊。而且我也出现在那本书里。好，我知道这书名。有一次我在 Colorado 的一家酒吧还是餐厅，跟一个人聊天，他问我在忙什么。

turns.en: He's like, oh, I'm writing this book on Boone Pickens. Yeah. Yeah. So, and he passed not so long ago, right? Was it a year ago? In September.
turns.zh: 他说：哦，我在写一本关于 Boone Pickens 的书。是啊是啊。他不久前去世了，对吧？是一年前吗？九月的时候。

turns.en: Yeah. September. He was, he, but he's, yeah, we had, I was real fortunate to get to spend time with him. And he was a good mentor and we, a good friend.
turns.zh: 对，九月。我很幸运能有机会和他相处，他是位好导师，也是位好朋友。

turns.en: And yeah, no, I was a Paul Barrett, his funeral. So we were, we were, that was nice to get that honor. And he, you know, he was a good guy and a lot of fun.
turns.zh: 是啊，我还在他葬礼上做了扶灵人（pallbearer），能获此殊荣真的很荣幸。他是好人，也非常有趣。

turns.en: We had fun together. Yeah. Oklahoma State Cowboy. That's it. That's it. That's it. So how did, how'd you go from Canadian Texas to becoming a hedge fund manager, for lack of a better word?
turns.zh: 我们在一起很开心。是啊，Oklahoma State 的牛仔，就是这样。那么，你是怎么从德州 Canadian 一路走到成为——暂且这么说——一名对冲基金管理人的？

turns.en: I don't know if you liked that moniker or not, but. Yeah. Well, no, it's, it's fine. That's, you know, I started, I started trading futures in college.
turns.zh: 我不知道你喜不喜欢这个称呼。还行，没关系。我是在大学时开始交易期货的。

turns.en: And so I was lucky to Jerry Parker. I'd met him through a family connection and he. Of Chesapeake family. Chesapeake. Yeah. Right. And so I was, I've always been, there's a lot of things I'm not good at, Jeff, but I am good at math and data and statistics.
turns.zh: 我很幸运，遇到了 Jerry Parker。我是通过一层亲戚关系认识他的，他……来自 Chesapeake 那一系。Chesapeake，对，没错。我一直觉得，Jeff，有很多事我不擅长，但数学、数据和统计我是擅长的。

turns.en: And so, so he had mentioned, and I know with studying finance at Notre Dame, and he had mentioned to me while I was about halfway through college, he had talked about what he does with basically technical analysis and basically using data to predict where markets may go.
turns.zh: 他跟我提过——那会儿我在 Notre Dame 学金融，大学读到一半时，他跟我讲过他在做的事，基本上就是技术分析（technical analysis），用数据来预测市场可能往哪走。

turns.en: He was there at Notre Dame or he was. He was, so I saw him and I met him in Canadian. So his, his first wife, she and I had mutual first cousins.
turns.zh: 他是在 Notre Dame 出现的吗？不是，我是在 Canadian 见到并认识他的。他的第一任妻子和我有共同的表亲。

turns.en: So we were at, we were at those mutual first cousins houses here at the house here in Canadian. And so I met him, the new husband to a cousin of a cousin.
turns.zh: 我们当时就在 Canadian 那位共同表亲家里。所以我认识了他——他是我表亲的表亲的新婚丈夫。

turns.en: And so he, he told me, he told me about trading and what he did. And I thought, wow, that's fascinating. And so he was an original turtle, right?
turns.zh: 他跟我讲了交易、讲了他做的事，我想：哇，太有意思了。他是最初的『海龟』（turtle）之一，对吧？

turns.en: And it was when he was a turtle. He was still working for Richard Dennis at the time. Oh, wow. So he said, Hey, well, you could come to Richmond and, and I could, you know, at least show you some of what I'm doing.
turns.zh: 那正是他当海龟的时候，当时他还在为 Richard Dennis 工作。哦，哇。他说：嘿，你可以来 Richmond，我至少可以给你看看我在做的一些东西。

turns.en: He was just being nice to the new, you know, here he comes and meets, you know, 30 people, his wife's family. And so I know he was just being nice to looking back.
turns.zh: 他其实就是对新人客气一下——他过来一下子要见三十来号人，都是他太太的家人。现在回头看，我知道他当时只是出于好意。

turns.en: But at the time I thought, Oh, okay, great. Well, so then, then about three days later, I'm on the phone to him said, Hey, when can I come to Richmond?
turns.zh: 但当时我想：哦，好啊，太好了。结果大概三天后，我就给他打电话说：嘿，我什么时候能来 Richmond？

turns.en: Well, he was probably the only one of the 30 that wanted to talk math instead of ranching. You know, I asked him, I said, Well, had anyone ever taken you up on that offer?
turns.zh: 估计那三十个人里，只有你想聊数学而不是聊牧场。我后来还问他：真有人答应过你这个提议吗？

turns.en: Because he had made this offer and it was, I guess, just an offer that no one says yes on, but I was excited to go hear about it. So he was nice to kind of show me some things and point me in the right direction.
turns.zh: 因为他抛出这个提议，我猜这大概是个没人会答应的客套邀请，但我却兴奋得很想去听听。所以他很好心，给我展示了一些东西，把我引上了正确的方向。

turns.en: And then so then I started trading during my last semester at college and then right out of college in, I got out a semester early with honors out at Notre Dame with a finance degree started in January of 88, managing money.
turns.zh: 于是我在大学最后一个学期开始交易，然后一毕业就入行——我提前一个学期以优等荣誉从 Notre Dame 毕业，拿了金融学位，从 88 年 1 月开始管理资金。

turns.en: But, you know, but it was interesting. I started in August of 87 with a $50,000 account. I was taking 21 hours at Notre Dame, a big load of classes.
turns.zh: 不过说来有意思，我是 87 年 8 月用一个 5 万美元的账户起步的。当时我在 Notre Dame 修了 21 个学分，课业很重。

turns.en: I was hurrying to try to get back to my now wife, my then girlfriend. My grandfather was back here with a job and he was a great guy to work with.
turns.zh: 我急着赶回来陪我现在的太太、当时的女朋友。我祖父在老家这边有份差事，和他共事很棒。

turns.en: And, but so the crash of 87 was two months in. And so that was an interesting time. So you were trading from college during the crash of 87.
turns.zh: 结果 87 年股灾在两个月后就来了，那段时间很有意思。所以你是在大学里、87 年股灾期间做交易的。

turns.en: So, you know, it's interesting like here we are now in the middle of the coronavirus crash. And it's, and, you know, we've had some crashes in between.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，如今我们正处在冠状病毒引发的崩盘之中，而这中间我们也经历过好几次崩盘。

turns.en: So crashes tend to, they're, they're each one a little unique, but they all rhyme to some degree. So there's probably some kid at Notre Dame or elsewhere right now trading some account.
turns.zh: 崩盘往往是这样：每一次都有点独特，但又都在某种程度上彼此押韵、似曾相识。所以现在大概在 Notre Dame 或别的什么地方，就有某个孩子在操盘某个账户。

turns.en: Yeah, I know. Doing something we're not even thinking about. Yeah, no, that's right. We're getting an education. I know that first crash in 87 was an education for me.
turns.zh: 是啊，我知道，在做一些我们压根想不到的事。对，没错，我们正在接受教育。我知道 87 年那场最初的崩盘对我就是一堂教育课。

turns.en: It was a, so the Euro dollar, the interest rate markets moved 37 standard deviation move. And, and, you know, I'd taken statistics about a year before.
turns.zh: 当时欧洲美元（Eurodollar）——也就是利率市场——出现了 37 个标准差的波动。而我大概一年前才修过统计学。

turns.en: And I thought, you know, they talk about one, two and three standard deviations and 99.7 is within three standard deviations. Well, it's that point three that's outside of three standard deviations really is the most important part.
turns.zh: 我就想，大家总在讲一个、两个、三个标准差，说 99.7% 都落在三个标准差之内。可恰恰是三个标准差之外那 0.3%，才是最重要的部分。

turns.en: And that's the part they never talk about because that's the part that breaks you or kills you is the, the, you know, that, that 0.3% outside of three standard deviations.
turns.zh: 而那正是他们从不谈及的部分，因为恰恰是那部分会把你击垮、要你的命——就是三个标准差之外的那 0.3%。

turns.en: And you think you understood that from that early point that the markets aren't normally distributed and they're, have these outlier moves? No, I, no, but when they took half my accounts value, I had a $50,000 account.
turns.zh: 那你从那么早就明白了市场并非正态分布、会有这些极端离群波动吗？不，我没那么早懂，但当它吞掉我账户一半的价值时——我当时是个 5 万美元的账户——

turns.en: It's sunk in a little bit. It went to 66,000 in two months and then the 33,000 on, on October 20th, 1987, that Tuesday was the day after the crash because the Euro dollar futures, that's when they moved up that 37 standard deviation move.
turns.zh: 就有点往心里去了。账户两个月里涨到 66000，然后在 1987 年 10 月 20 日那个周二、也就是股灾后的第二天，跌到了 33000，因为欧洲美元期货正是那时候出现了那 37 个标准差的上冲。

turns.en: So no, but, and it takes a while for some of that to sink in. So you don't realize it right away, but I did know it was a historic event. I was lucky to survive without, you know, without losing all my money.
turns.zh: 所以，这些领悟是要花一段时间才慢慢消化的，你不会马上就明白。但我确实知道那是个历史性事件。我很幸运活了下来，没有把本钱全赔光。

turns.en: And, and I tried, you try to model where you're doing is trend following. I was trading 21 markets and trend, a trend following model. It was a turtle version version.
turns.zh: 我当时尝试去建模，做的就是趋势跟踪。我在 21 个市场上用一个趋势跟踪模型交易，那是一个『海龟』的改版。

turns.en: Kind of a turtle version. Yeah. Yeah. And then said, all right, I'm coming back to Canadian. I'm going to do this for a living. Right. Right.
turns.zh: 算是海龟的一个变种。是啊。然后我说：好，我要回 Canadian，把这个当成职业来做。对，对。

turns.en: You know, my back of a 50% drawdown. Right. Yeah. My grandfather, he said, of all the ways to lose money, why in the heck do you have to pick the very fastest one?
turns.zh: 带着 50% 回撤的战绩回去。对，是啊。我祖父说：在所有亏钱的法子里，你为什么偏偏要挑最快的那一种？

turns.en: So he was a businessman. He'd been, he had done deals all his life in oil and gas. And he had seen, you know, he was a, he was an interesting deal maker guy that he was just great.
turns.zh: 他是个生意人，一辈子都在石油天然气行业做交易、谈买卖。他见识广，是个很有意思的、极棒的交易者。

turns.en: So. The oil and gas to me always is a good corollary to trend following and to, right? Cause you're digging a lot of holes that don't pay off, but doesn't cost a lot.
turns.zh: 在我看来，石油天然气一直是趋势跟踪的一个绝好类比，对吧？因为你挖了很多不出油的井、回报为零，但每口的成本又不高。

turns.en: And then boom, when one hits, you got this huge outlier, outlier gain. So it's lumpy, like a classic trend following would be. Absolutely. Yeah.
turns.zh: 然后突然一下，一口井出油了，你就得到一笔巨大的离群收益。所以它是一阵一阵的、块状的，就像经典的趋势跟踪那样。完全正确。是的。

turns.en: No, it's a, it's an interesting, there's a lot of parallels to risk management and diversification applied to oil and gas very much. So how to side topic, how are all those people doing in the current I tell you, it's, you know, it's really bad.
turns.zh: 这很有意思，风险管理和分散化在石油天然气行业有很多相通之处。那岔个话题，眼下这行里的人都过得怎么样？我告诉你，真的很糟。

turns.en: I mean, right now it's worse than 86. So 86 and 14 are both kind of parallel to me. But right now we've gone from bad to incredibly bad. You know, there's literally, there's people with oil right now in the last 48 hours there have been, I've been hearing stories of just shutting in wells, just go turn off wells to say, look, we're, we're not even selling the oil and the gas.
turns.zh: 我是说，现在比 86 年还糟。86 年和 14 年在我看来有点相似，但现在我们已经从糟糕滑向糟糕透顶。真的有产油的人，在过去 48 小时里，我一直听到有直接关停油井的故事——就是去把井关掉，意思是：看，我们连油和气都不卖了。

turns.en: Usually that they at least produce what they've already drilled. They stopped drilling new wells, but they at least produce what they're doing.
turns.zh: 通常他们至少还会开采已经钻好的井，会停止钻新井，但起码还会维持现有产能。

turns.en: But I think I read today, we're rallying today and because of that, because they're just shutting down production. Yeah. Yeah. And they, I mean, literally I know people who are out, the guys that, what they call pumpers and they go, they're turning off wells.
turns.zh: 但我今天好像读到，市场今天在反弹，正是因为这个——因为他们在直接关停产能。是啊是啊。我是说，我真的认识一些人，就是他们所说的『采油工』（pumpers），他们跑去把油井一口口关掉。

turns.en: We've got a company on a, you know, and I invest some to an oil and gas as well. And we've got a company that is saying, we're not sure we were even going to buy any oil from you.
turns.zh: 我自己也投了一些石油天然气。有一家公司直接说：我们不确定还会不会从你们这儿买油了。

turns.en: They canceled our contract two days ago. And so they just say, you know, and, you know, you could, and then you see $20 oil on the futures, but it's out in the field. It's like $10 oil.
turns.zh: 他们两天前取消了和我们的合同。你在期货上看到的是 20 美元的油价，但到了油田现场，实际大概只有 10 美元。

turns.en: Really? So it's not, yeah, you've got this big basis differential and then jet fuel. I'm reading they don't even have enough places to put all the unused jet fuel.
turns.zh: 真的？所以，是的，中间有这么大的基差（basis）。还有航空燃油，我看到说他们甚至没有足够的地方来存放所有用不完的航空燃油。

turns.en: Right. So it's not enough physical storage out there in the world. Yeah. No oil and gas is going to be really hurt. You know, there'll be like, if you had a restaurant, you could see in six months, you go open the restaurant back up, everybody's back to work.
turns.zh: 对，全世界没有足够的实物存储空间。是啊。石油天然气这行会受到重创。这就好比如果你开一家餐厅，你能预见到六个月后重新开张、大家重新上岗。

turns.en: But oil and gas, you know, you're really, you know, you're, it's bad for six months, but it's going to be bad for another six to 12 months because of all this excess supply that's been stuck everywhere.
turns.zh: 但石油天然气不一样，它糟糕六个月，可因为到处都积压着这么多过剩供应，它还要再糟糕六到十二个月。

turns.en: Right. And you're not, no one's putting the investment in right now. No, no. So the, and that's on top of 18 months of terrible MLP and whole industries had a tough go of it.
turns.zh: 对，而且现在没人在往里投钱。没有没有。这还是在 MLP（master limited partnership，主限合伙）已经惨淡了 18 个月的基础上雪上加霜，整个行业都过得很艰难。

turns.en: Yeah. No, we've really gone from bad to not worse, bad to horrible. I mean, really, I've never seen it in my lifetime. This bad. I saw 86 was bad, 14 was bad, oh, eight was bad and back.
turns.zh: 是啊。我们真的从糟糕滑向了不是更糟、而是惨不忍睹。说真的，我这辈子从没见过这么糟的时候。我经历过 86 年很糟、14 年很糟、08 年很糟，还有更早的时候。

turns.en: It was that V drop, but this is, I mean, this has gone to a point where it's just catastrophic for the oil and gas business, but in a business really that's used to booms and busts.
turns.zh: 那次是个 V 型急跌，但这一次，我是说，已经到了对石油天然气行业堪称灾难性的地步，而这个行业本来就是习惯了大起大落的。

turns.en: So. Yeah. Well, God speed to those guys. Oh, yeah. So then you're there and what, so you started in your 86, eight, once you got back to Canadian started managing money and that was just small friends and family and whatnot.
turns.zh: 是啊，只能祝那些人好运了。哦是的。那你回到 Canadian 之后，就在 86、88 年前后开始管理资金，起初只是替亲友管点小钱之类的。

turns.en: Right. Right. My two brothers and my grandfather and me and yeah, my grandfather, he said it was, so he had his, his provision was I put in 45,000 and then two brothers put in 10 and 15.
turns.zh: 对对。是我两个兄弟、我祖父和我。我祖父当时定的条件是：我出 45000，两个兄弟分别出 10000 和 15000。

turns.en: And so I had 30,000. My grandfather put in to round out the 100,000 and, and I mean, he would, I mean, this is a guy who would go drill a half million dollar well and, and come up zero.
turns.zh: 所以我出 30000，我祖父补足到 10 万。要知道，他可是那种会去钻一口 50 万美元的井、结果一无所获的人。

turns.en: So 30,000 is kind of in 88. So chump change, chump change if to him, so he was a real wheeler dealer and did. And so he said to me, he said, he said, okay, I'll put the 30,000, but if you get down to half, if we lose half our money, we stop this commodity trading nonsense, throw that quote machine out the window and get back to real business.
turns.zh: 所以在 88 年，3 万美元对他来说就是点小钱、零头。他是个真正精明会来事儿的生意人。他对我说：好吧，我出这 3 万，但如果亏到只剩一半、亏掉一半本钱，我们就别玩这套商品交易的鬼把戏了，把那台报价机扔出窗外，回去做正经生意。

turns.en: And so I said, okay, so that's January of 88. Well, it was funny then. So January, well, February, March, April, May, it's, it's going down 81,000.
turns.zh: 我说好。那是 88 年 1 月。然后就好笑了。1 月、2 月、3 月、4 月、5 月，一路往下跌到 81000。

turns.en: I start May. Well, May, the first 10 days of May were bad. And, and I'm down to just above 70,000. Well, then I remember about mid May, because I was hoping would stay above 70,000.
turns.zh: 到了 5 月，5 月头十天很糟，我跌到只剩 7 万出头。我记得大概 5 月中旬，因为我一直盼着能守住 7 万这条线。

turns.en: Well, it dropped below 70 and I'd get this fax in, you know, those curled up fax machines from a thermal paper. Yeah, whatever that paper was.
turns.zh: 结果它跌破了 7 万，我就收到一份传真，就是那种用热敏纸、会卷起来的传真机打出来的。是啊，管它是什么纸呢。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah, that's right. And so he comes in my office, sticks his head in that morning. He said, where are we today? And I said, 68,742 dollars.
turns.zh: 是啊是啊，没错。那天早上他把头探进我办公室，问：今天多少了？我说：68742 美元。

turns.en: And he's just a matter of time. He wanted to get you into the oil business. Oh yeah. He was like, let's stop this junk. And this is a waste of time.
turns.zh: 他就等着这一天呢。他就是想把你拉回石油行当。哦是的。他就说：别搞这些垃圾了，纯属浪费时间。

turns.en: And you're, you know, and I remember I showed him a big, a big simulation. I said, look, granddad, if I had done this, look how much money I'd have made over this year.
